newsitem.title: UK: P&I insurer says keep $20 bln marine cover limit.
newsitem.headline: P&I insurer says keep $20 bln marine cover limit.

text.p: Protection & Indemnity (P&I) insurer The Standard Club said on Monday that insurance cover for marine liability claims should not be reduced from its current maximum of around $20 billion.
"The Club is in favour of maintaining the status quo, which it believes provides shipowners with the cheapest long-term liability insurance," it said in a statement on Monday.

P&I clubs are mutual insurers providing liability cover for the bulk of world shipping. Some members of the so-called P&I Group, which includes most of the clubs, believe that the limit should be reduced.
They fear that a so-called overspill call from a major liability claim could bankrupt the shipping industry.

However, The Standard argues that the industry could support a claim of up to $20 billion and supports its case with a report jointly commissioned from the Maritime Economics Research Centre of the Netherlands.

"The report from the MERC explains that, although the cost of an overspill call could be substantial, a call would be collectable without serious disruptions over the likely time-frame that such a call would be required."
